limitations: No concurrent builds or tests from this task during measurements; unrelated host activity was not stopped.
The original-engine baseline has one sample; current one/four-thread and IDA results have three samples per entry.
The baseline restores all modified engine sources to the baseline commit using the same LLVM r4 toolchain.
NeverD source text and Hex-Rays pseudocode use different presentation formats; output quality is not normalized.
A matching complete source hash establishes text reproducibility, not semantic equivalence to the input.
Worker timings do not measure Qt painting or hardware presentation.

caveats: Warm OS caches; each entry starts a fresh worker/database.
NeverD: first 256 source lines and all subsequent pages, including IPC.
IDA: fresh auto-analysis, then decompile() and complete text.
Wall-clock measurements include other host activity; load is recorded.
Source hashes check reproducibility, not semantic equivalence to the binary.
